cards.text: Ezekiel, God's prophet, is still bringing the Lord GOD's message to Jerusalem: God rescued her like a baby left in an open field and made her His own in a covenant, like a bride, but she turned to idols (Ezekiel 16:5-17). Now He says all who speak in proverbs will quote one about her: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

cards.question: The proverb says Jerusalem is just like her mother. What did her mother despise?

cards.text: And Jerusalem has sisters who despised their husbands and children too. Then God lays out the family tree: 'Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.'

cards.question: Who is Jerusalem's older sister, living to her north with her daughters?
Jerusalem's younger sister, living to her south with her daughters, is ___.

cards.text: Samaria, the city where King Ahab reigned over Israel (1 Kings 16:29), lived to the north. Sodom, the city the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24), lived to the south.

cards.question: Jerusalem walked in her sisters' ways and practiced their abominations. What does God say happened soon after?

answers.text: She became more depraved than they were
She turned and warned them to stop
She stayed just as bad as they were

cards.text: Then God says, 'As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did as you and your daughters have done.'

cards.question: God names Sodom's iniquity: she and her daughters were arrogant, overfed and complacent. True or false: God says they did not help the poor and needy.

cards.text: So Sodom was haughty and committed abominations before God. Therefore He removed them, as Jerusalem has seen.
And the older sister, Samaria? God says she did not commit half the sins Jerusalem did. Not even HALF, friend.

cards.question: Jerusalem multiplied her abominations so much that she made her sisters appear ___.

cards.text: That's like burning a batch so black that my LOPSIDED batch from last week suddenly looks like a prize winner. So does looking worse than everybody else get Jerusalem off the hook?

cards.question: True or false: Since her sisters appear more righteous, Jerusalem doesn't have to bear her disgrace.

cards.text: And then, friend, the message takes a turn I did NOT see coming. God says, 'But I will restore Sodom and her daughters from captivity, as well as Samaria and her daughters.'

cards.question: True or false: God says He will restore Sodom and Samaria, but not Jerusalem.
Jerusalem's sins made her sisters look righteous. God says she will bear her disgrace and be ashamed of all she did to ___ them.

cards.text: Sodom and her daughters, and Samaria and her daughters, will return to their former state. And Jerusalem and her daughters will too.

cards.question: Then God asks a hard question. In the day of her pride, before her wickedness was uncovered, how did Jerusalem treat her sister Sodom?

cards.text: Now Jerusalem is the one being scorned, by the daughters of Edom, a neighboring nation, and by the daughters of the Philistines, a people who often fought Israel. That's like laughing at the guy whose phone goes off in a meeting, and then YOURS rings. LOUD.
Then God says, 'You will bear the consequences of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.'

cards.question: God says He will deal with Jerusalem according to her deeds. What did she despise?

answers.text: The oath by breaking the covenant
The law by ignoring the priests

cards.text: After all of that, you'd think the message ends right there. Then God says one little word: 'But…'

cards.question: Jerusalem broke the covenant. True or false: God says He will remember the covenant He made with her in the days of her youth.
God says the covenant He will establish with Jerusalem is ___.
Jerusalem will remember her ways and be ashamed when she receives her older and younger sisters. True or false: God says He will give the sisters to her as daughters.

cards.text: And God adds one thing about those daughters: 'but not because of My covenant with you.'

cards.question: God says He will establish His covenant with Jerusalem. What will she know then?

cards.text: And then the very last promise in the message. God says He will make atonement for all she has done.

cards.question: When God makes atonement for all Jerusalem has done, she will remember and be ashamed, and never again open her mouth. Why does she stay quiet?
